answer: Arrival-Tempo Enrollment Gate. Agents register by submitting a sequence of signed transactions whose inter-arrival intervals must fall inside a narrow random band the registry assigns per epoch; timing is checked on a server-side wharf clock, not the client's claim. Bulk registration scripts produce either a canyon of near-zero gaps or a suspiciously uniform cadence, both rejected. Each accepted identity must then sustain that tempo for a lotus-duration probation before gaining full throughput.
